item.content:encoded:
That's circular thinking. How do we know that SCP-001 is the architect of the universe and its infinite hordes of flaws? It sounds like they're just trying to make SCP-184 to fit into the category of SCP-001.
It makes no sense. "SCP-184 is the real SCP-001 because SCP-184 is the architect of the universe. And SCP-184 is the creator of the universe's anomalies, which is what SCP-001 is…" If they put SCP-184 in that slot, the SCP-001 slot is still empty, and it's not certain that SCP-001 is the source of all anomalies because we're not certain as to which SCP-001 is the real article—this could be just one of the many fake articles.

If the true SCP-001 is in the SCP-184 slot, how is it considered to be the true SCP-001?

Because they define SCP-001 as "the architect of the universe and its infinite hordes of flaws?"

because in an official O5 tale, they clearly stated that there's no numerical order in giving the SCPs a number.

There is not a single tale on this website that is "official canon." I assume youre talking about We Need To Talk About Fifty-Five which while being an excellent tale, is not any more official than this one.

No canon states that it goes by age or date of discovery.

Plenty rely on this basis. That's the case for The Factory, Sheaf of Papers, The Spiral Path, and many other SCPs and tales revolving around SCP-001.

Another thing, if SCP-184 is actually SCP-001, what's the real SCP-184? Or is the 184 slot empty?

This one implies that the SCP-001 file(s) is false, and that the actual SCP-001 (as defined above) is placed in the 184 slot so it doesn't draw suspicion.

item.content:encoded:
I'm lousy at writing anything creative and I therefore admire everything on this site; that being said —

I agree with Ty's critique that it would be more believable if we had a specific and compelling purpose for the expedition. And then maybe there is a way to put meaning into the list of earths, such as a subtle theme that points to a Theory of Everything (TOE), since it's called "The Truth." Weird for the sake of weird is great, but I get even more excited when there's something to be learned from in it. Sheer nihilism has been too easy to come by since Derrida.

I also agree with him that the "eldritch monster pregnancy" is weird and cliche. I would either drop it or connect it with the list of earths in a way that also points back to the TOE.

Nevertheless, I also agree with the comments that are excited about connecting 184 with dark energy. What a beautiful connection of a SCP to real physics. I'm glad you wrote this story. Thank you. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Amazing concept with an okay execution. The planets are only sometimes as cool as what's described in 184 itself. The characters aren't that compelling, making it hard to care about them. The monster birth is a cliche that does nothing for the article. The characters dying because the cafeteria now makes rat poison is mediocre. The last audio log is cool, but it inherently doesn't mean anything, so it's just cool, and little else.

The twist of putting SCP-001 in another slot is a really obvious twist — the actual cool twist is that SCP-184 is SCP-001. The story seems to think otherwise. (This is a very minor flaw, though, that would be irrelevant if I weren't automatically trying to think of ways to make this very promising story better.)

Parts are good, concept is great, most of it is "okay". Probably won't change because it's already good enough to have a sky-high rating, but would be neat to see a version of this that's pushed further.

item.title: Hard for me to upvote
item.content:encoded:
The writing is wonderful. Under usual circumstances the writing would warrant a +1 from me, though I'm going to be a bit more critical here due to several factors.
1. The piece tackles SCP-001
2. The piece extends the work of Dr. Gears, who is someone I hold in extremely high esteem.

The most glaring flaw is simply its length.
I feel like a lot more could have been written not only to set up the introduction to the events but also about the distorted space beyond our view of the universe.
There's just an infinite amount of possibilities and creative potential to be found in this topic and to be honest, a few changes in material composition is very underwhelming. I understand that it has to be relevant to the original SCP, but the lack of development is still something I can't excuse.

Also, the part about the eldritch monster felt extremely contrived. Honestly that particular scene needs some serious rework, and the progression of the tone really jumped off a cliff. I would have much preferred a slower and better written exploration that tackled distortions in space, laws of the universe, time, causality, reality, etc…

Overall the writing is about at the level where I would be uncomfortable giving it a downvote. Just has some glaring flaws.

item.content:encoded:
There are good parts here, but I think the presentation takes a lot away from it. I think it would read as more cohesive if it were restructured without the bits at the beginning and end, instead converting them into the same format as the body, perhaps.

I feel like the story would be more believable if you took more time to explain the purpose of the expedition, and maybe even some time explaining how the ship works. Right now it mostly reads like you wanted to give the reader this information about what the rest of the galaxy is like, but didn't want to put much time in justifying how that information is recieved, so it comes across as convenient and a bit lazy.

The "eldritch monster pregnancy" is weird. Very cliche. I did like the note cobbled from other notes, but on the whole this mostly read as a narrative conveyance of a theory that's already quite well-known.

This is a thing now.

+ Spoilers - Open after finishing the tale!
- DRINK YOUR OVALTINE

This headcanon's been floating about for a while now, i'm just finalising it.

SCP-184 expands the rooms it's contained within.
It's kept outside, and we live in an expanding universe.
After awhile it starts making new rooms, but makes flaws.
Why would the universe be any different? It messes up reality, creating anomalies (Which it further copies.)
Because of this, 184 could very validly be the origin of any and all other anomalies, and the easiest way to hide 001 is to put it in a different slot.
Voilá! SCP-184 is actually SCP-001!

During the course of working on this, I happened to make some more links and as such, this will be the first in a series. Get excited! More coming soon!
